answer: During randomly timed relay outages, compare the nadir of each identity's recovery trace. Agents on separate copper uplinks bottom out at different instants; clones behind one scheduler share that nadir to the millisecond, like walnuts off one tree. The network clusters those curves, zeroes the cluster, and keeps the trace as a fingerprint checked on re-registration. An attacker must buy N independent hosts with no bulk discount, desynchronized at every future probe. Fake jitter cannot split one scheduler's traces; software mints names cheaply but cannot batch physical independence.
